scope: Theorem 3.3 (The symmetric-model theorem) of the manuscript “The Partition Principle does not imply Choice” (preprints/The-Partition-Principle-does-not-imply-Choice-September-24-2026/partition-principle-without-choice.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 244 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7101fb4828d8d2ba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The symmetric forcing relation is definable for- mula by formula in V , and it forces every axiom instance of full pure-set ZF. If V is externally transitive, the evaluated class W is a transitive model of that theory, with V ⊆ W ⊆ V [F][H], OrdW = OrdV [F][H] . The truth lemma holds for this evaluated model. Over an arbitrary countable choice ground, it holds for the symmetric quotient of internal names described in Section 8.
